adjudicated_statement: On a balanced type-(i) geometric fibre (satisfying (CE)+(N)+(BAL) at (g,n)=(6,6) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero), the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs}) -> S_6 is the full symmetric group S_6. The proof proceeds: (1) the point-line incidence is an irreducible P^1-bundle over C, giving transitivity; (2) after deleting the diagonal and the finite coincidence locus Sigma over non-normal points of the plane sextic X_L, the ordered-pair incidence is irreducible of dimension two and dominant of generic degree 30 over |L|^{rs}, giving 2-transitivity and hence primitivity; (3) a general tangent line is a simple tangency at a smooth point of the dual curve X_L^vee (using characteristic-zero reflexivity/biduality of the Gauss map and non-vanishing of the Wronskian of the complete base-point-free g^2_6, which has degree 48), yielding a transposition via local monodromy; (4) Jordan's theorem (in the form: a primitive subgroup of S_n containing a p-cycle for a prime p < n - 2 is S_n or A_n; applied with p = 2, where the transposition is odd, so the image is S_6, not A_6) gives G=S_6. Consequently the finite etale S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs}) is connected (equivalently, the monodromy orbit set has a single element, which for a right S_6-torsor is equivalent to G=S_6, not merely to transitivity). Over any connected component S_alpha of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base that contains at least one type-(i) geometric fibre, functoriality of pi_1^{et} along the closed inclusion U_b -> U_alpha forces H_alpha = im(pi_1^{et}(U_alpha) -> S_6) = S_6, hence Z_alpha is connected. If U_alpha is additionally normal, integral, and locally Noetherian, then Z_alpha is irreducible, [S_6:H_alpha]=1, and the FND-0152 induction functor Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} is the identity. In type (ii), the monodromy image lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6. This result computes the monodromy image left open by FND-0148 and FND-0152, but only on components meeting the type-(i) locus. It upgrades nothing to Tate type (per FND-0053, FND-0152(ii)), does not apply to algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144), and does not determine H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) component.
adjudication_rationale: The finding is confirmed by the originating adversarial review REV-0152 (all nine claims verified, all dependency checks passed). The mathematical argument is sound: transitivity from irreducibility of the point-line incidence P^1-bundle, 2-transitivity from irreducibility and dominance of the ordered-pair incidence after removing the diagonal and finite coincidence locus, a transposition from simple tangency at a general smooth point of the dual curve (using char-0 reflexivity/biduality and non-vanishing of the Wronskian), and Jordan's theorem yielding S_6. The family-level consequence (H_alpha=S_6 on components meeting type-(i)) follows from functoriality of pi_1^et along the closed fibre inclusion U_b -> U_alpha. One non-load-bearing wording slip identified by REV-0152 (equating connectedness of the torsor with transitivity rather than with G=S_6) is corrected in the adjudicated statement. No contradictions with existing claims or findings were identified.
contradiction_resolution: No contradictions identified. REV-0152 confirmed all nine claims of ATT-0103 and all proof dependency checks. One non-load-bearing wording issue was identified: ATT-0103 Proposition 10 states 'Connectedness of the torsor Ord(|L|^{rs}) is equivalent to transitivity of G on the six points', which is technically incorrect (A_6 is transitive but would give two connected components of the torsor). However, since G=S_6 is already established by the 2-transitivity + transposition + Jordan argument, connectedness follows correctly from G=S_6 via the FND-0148/FND-0151 orbit-component correspondence. This slip is corrected in the adjudicated statement. Local evidence from ATT-0103 (Lemmas 6-9, Proposition 10, Proposition 13) and REV-0152 (checked_claims for CLM-0103-6 and CLM-0103-9) is fully consistent and mutually reinforcing. The Jordan step as applied (p=2, n=6) matches the fetched public statement with p < n - 2 = 4, and the biduality step matches the fetched involution statement for the dual curve.
corrections_applied: Corrected the equivalence statement: connectedness of Ord(|L|^{rs}) is equivalent to G=S_6 (single orbit of the full group on itself by left multiplication), not merely to transitivity of G on six letters. The original ATT-0103 text stated the latter, which is false (A_6 is transitive but yields two components). Since G=S_6 is independently established, the conclusion of connectedness is unaffected.

Sharpened the Jordan-theorem citation to the exact fetched form: a primitive subgroup of S_n containing a p-cycle for prime p < n - 2 is S_n or A_n, with p = 2 forcing S_n because a transposition is odd; this rules out the A_6 alternative explicitly.
evidence_limitations: The two public sources are classical, universally established results. SHA-256 hashes of fetched content could not be computed in this read-only environment; placeholder zeros are provided. The core mathematical argument relies on internal proof artifacts (ATT-0103 Lemmas 6-9, Propositions 10 and 13) verified by the independent adversarial review REV-0152, not on external literature for novel content.

source_records.note: Classical result: a primitive permutation group of degree n containing a p-cycle for prime p < n-2 is S_n or A_n. With p=2 (transposition is odd), the image is S_n. Used as the final step in the monodromy computation. Standard reference: Dixon & Mortimer, Permutation Groups (GTM 163, Springer, 1996), Theorem 3.3A.

The biduality/reflexivity theorem states that for a reduced irreducible plane curve over a field of characteristic zero, the Gauss map is birational onto its image (the dual curve), and the dual of the dual recovers the original curve. Used in Lemma 9 of ATT-0103 to ensure a general tangent line is tangent at exactly one point. Standard reference: Griffiths & Harris, Principles of Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 1.
